name: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn Bashshār al-Anbārī
summary: Thaʿlab's student and the last great Kufan of Baghdad, famed for his memory; author of books on the pause in the Qurʾān, on words of opposite meanings and on the masculine and feminine.
bio: Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī learnt from his father and from Thaʿlab and taught in Baghdad; al-Zubaydī places him in the sixth Kufan generation. The sources tell of his memory: thousands of verses cited as evidence for the Qurʾān, and the commentaries of the Qurʾān with their chains, all from memory. He is not the later Abū al-Barakāt ibn al-Anbārī, author of al-Inṣāf.

His Īḍāḥ al-waqf wa-l-ibtidāʾ, on where a reader of the Qurʾān may pause and begin, his al-Aḍdād and his al-Mudhakkar wa-l-muʾannath are still printed. Abū ʿAlī al-Qālī was his student and carried his books to Cordoba. He died in 328/940.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 79 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
